ribbondesc: Advancing the frontiers of computational multiphysics through innovative research and cutting-edge numerical methods.

High-Performance Computing & Solver Deve.title: High-Performance Computing & Solver Development
High-Performance Computing & Solver Deve.subtitle: Adaptive, Scalable, and Multiphysics-Ready
High-Performance Computing & Solver Deve.overview: Core lab effort: developing exascale-ready solvers built on Adaptive Mesh Refinement (AMR) and a Hybrid Sharp–Diffuse Interface Framework. These solver technologies underpin our shock hydrocodes, all-speed CFD, and multiscale frameworks.
currentProjects: AMR-enabled hydrocodes
Density-based all-speed solver framework
Hybrid Sharp–Diffuse Interface methods integrated with AMR
impact: Exascale-ready implementations for large HPC centers
Unified solver frameworks that span Mach regimes and multiphase problems
Reusable libraries and software components for group projects
High-Performance Computing & Solver Deve.imgtitle: Micro-turbojet with rotating compressor and turbine (top) and a rotating detonation engine (bottom), both from the group's in-house solver

High-Performance Computing & Solver Deve.title: In-House Computational Thermophysics Solver Development
High-Performance Computing & Solver Deve.subtitle: High-Strain-Rate Physics and Shock Physics Dynamics
High-Performance Computing & Solver Deve.overview: Scalable Computational Thermophysics Solver for shock propagation, impact and fragmentation problems. Designed to resolve sharp features while remaining robust in mixed-material zones using the hybrid interface approach.
currentProjects: Modeling shock initiation in energetic materials
Impact response of layered protective structures
High-order methods and AMR for shock-focused multiphysics
impact: Accurate prediction of shock–material interactions
Improved designs for protective systems and planetary entry models
Bridging experiments and simulations for validation

High-Performance Computing & Solver Deve.title: PyAMorph: Tool for Implicit Geometry Modeling & Morphometric Analysis
High-Performance Computing & Solver Deve.subtitle: Massively Parallel SDF Framework on Adaptive Meshes
High-Performance Computing & Solver Deve.overview: Signed Distance Functions (SDFs), Constructive Solid Geometry (CSG), and AMReX Adaptive Mesh Refinement for high-fidelity microstructure characterisation.
currentProjects: Implicit geometry modeling via SDFs and CSG operations
Chan-Vese segmentation for image-to-SDF conversion
TPMS metamaterial generation: Gyroid, Schwarz P/D, Neovius, BCC/FCC lattices
Automated morphometry for SDFs
impact: Enables simulation-ready microstructure geometry for solid propellant and metamaterial studies
Unified API composing images, STL meshes, and analytic shapes in a single CSG environment
Automated statistical morphometry over particle ensembles
Scalable to large HPC systems via AMReX domain decomposition without memory bottlenecks
High-Performance Computing & Solver Deve.imgtitle: 3D porous microstructure reconstructed via Chan-Vese segmentation on an AMReX MultiFab grid

High-Performance Computing & Solver Deve.title: Lumina: An AI-Augmented Multiscale Material Informatics Framework
High-Performance Computing & Solver Deve.subtitle: Activate-on-Demand Material Data for Extreme Aero-Chemo-Thermo-Mechanical Regimes
High-Performance Computing & Solver Deve.overview: A modular Python-based informatics framework that centralizes fragmented multiscale material data—from atomistic simulation datasets to macro-scale experimental records—within a unified repository utilizing a hierarchical XML schema and a conversational AI assistant.
currentProjects: Hierarchical XML-based schema and runtime material parsing architecture
Three-layer data state management (Original, Override, and Active views) for sandbox experimentation
Digitization of Shock Hugoniot databases (e.g., LANL reports) and multi-scale physics integration (Mie-Grüneisen and JWL Equations of State)
Conversational AI assistant utilizing locally deployed LLMs for natural language data querying
impact: Bridges the gap between granular atomistic data and continuum-scale hydrodynamic solvers through a traceable three-level parametric chain
Empowers formulators and simulation engineers with automated constitutive model validation and visualization (DoE stabilization)
Provides a stateless, header-only C++ execution backend suitable for highly concurrent HPC and parallel engineering environments
Enables completely offline, domain-expert-free database querying via automated natural-language-to-SQL conversions
High-Performance Computing & Solver Deve.imgtitle: Material Data Processing and AI-Based Natural Language Query Workflow with three-layer state mapping

Energetic Materials & Reactive Systems.title: Energetic Materials & Reactive Systems
Energetic Materials & Reactive Systems.subtitle: Initiation, Hot-Spot Physics, and Microstructure-aware burn models
Energetic Materials & Reactive Systems.overview: Multiscale, multiphysics study of energetic materials from atomistic chemistry to continuum-scale initiation and run-to-detonation behavior. We combine DFT, MD, KMC and continuum reactive flow models for predictive capabilities.
currentProjects: Hot-spot formation and growth in heterogeneous energetic materials
Reactive burn models coupled to hydrocodes
Multiscale Framework: DFT → MD → continuum
impact: Mechanistic insight into initiation and sensitivity
Improved constitutive/reaction models for engineering simulations
Data-driven parameter calibration linking experiments and simulation

Energetic Materials & Reactive Systems.title: Solid Propellant Modelling
Energetic Materials & Reactive Systems.subtitle: From Packed Microstructure to Burn Rate and Grain Integrity
Energetic Materials & Reactive Systems.overview: Predictive modelling of composite solid propellants starting from the microstructure: we pack realistic oxidiser particles, resolve the burning surface and the flame above it, and follow heat and stress into the solid to study burn rate, cracks and debonding.
currentProjects: Packing of spherical and faceted crystals to measured loadings
Interface-resolved burning of ammonium perchlorate propellants and burn-rate prediction
Coupled thermal and mechanical response of the burning solid
Grain geometry, burn-back and the effect of cracks and debonds
impact: Burn-rate trends predicted from measured material constants
Microstructures built to a recipe and validated against published packs
A route from CT images of real propellant to simulation
Energetic Materials & Reactive Systems.imgtitle: Packed propellant microstructures with faceted and spherical particles built with PyAMorph (top), and temperature and stress on a burning surface (bottom)

Impact-Resistant & Protective Materials.title: Impact-Resistant & Protective Materials
Impact-Resistant & Protective Materials.subtitle: Multiscale Mechanics and Materials Design for Protection
Impact-Resistant & Protective Materials.overview: Design and simulation of materials and structures optimized for impact resistance — from microstructural tailoring to structural-scale response — using coupled multiscale mechanics and dynamic testing calibration.
currentProjects: Multiscale models for fiber-matrix composites under impact
Topology and microstructure optimization for energy absorption
Coupling experiments and simulations for validation
impact: Guides design of lighter, more effective protective systems
Translates microstructural design rules to engineering-scale performance
Supports defense and aerospace material qualification
Impact-Resistant & Protective Materials.imgtitle: Bullet-on-armour geometry built with PyAMorph (top) and a hypervelocity debris impact on a bumper shield simulated in-house (bottom)

Bioinspired Materials & Structures.title: Bioinspired Materials & Structures
Bioinspired Materials & Structures.subtitle: Origami, Architected Lattices and Nature's Armour
Bioinspired Materials & Structures.overview: Nature folds, layers and grades its structures to absorb energy and change shape. We model origami-based structures and architected materials inspired by biology — Kresling cells, spinodoid and cuttlebone-like lattices, nacre-like layups and fibre armour — under impact, blast and aerodynamic loading.
currentProjects: Origami (Kresling) cells as foldable, energy-absorbing structures under blast
Bistable origami wings that change shape in a gust
Spinodoid and graded porous architectures as shields against orbital-debris impact
Bioinspired UHMWPE–Kevlar armour and cuttlebone-like lattices
impact: Lightweight structures that fold, snap and absorb energy by design
Geometry generators for origami and architected materials that feed directly into simulation
Design rules for protective structures in aerospace and defence
Bioinspired Materials & Structures.imgtitle: A folding Kresling origami cell (top) and a spinodoid architecture built with PyAMorph (bottom)

Fluid–Structure Interaction.title: Fluid–Structure Interaction & Moving Bodies
Fluid–Structure Interaction.subtitle: Two-Way Coupled Flow and Deforming Structures
Fluid–Structure Interaction.overview: Many of our problems have a structure that moves or deforms because of the flow, and a flow that changes because of it. Our in-house solver couples compressible and incompressible flow to thin shells, membranes and rigid multibody motion through sharp immersed interfaces on adaptive meshes.
currentProjects: Origami wing in a turning stream: tip vortex, wake and snap-through
Blast loading of a thin-walled origami cell with a shell finite-element model
Flapping and rotating bodies: insect flight, rotors and turbomachinery
Deployable and inflatable decelerators in supersonic flow
impact: One framework for rigid, articulated and flexible bodies in high- and low-speed flow
Thin structures resolved without body-fitted remeshing
Simulations that reach flight-relevant Reynolds and Mach numbers on GPUs
Fluid–Structure Interaction.imgtitle: Two-way coupled simulation of a bistable origami wing with its tip vortex (top) and an origami cell under a blast wave (bottom)

Hypersonic & Reentry Physics.title: Hypersonic & Reentry Physics
Hypersonic & Reentry Physics.subtitle: Ablation, Aerothermochemistry, and Plasma–Material Interaction
Hypersonic & Reentry Physics.overview: Coupled study of high-enthalpy aerothermodynamics, surface ablation and chemistry, and plasma–material interactions encountered during hypersonic flight and planetary reentry.
currentProjects: Ablation and surface chemistry modelling for TPS materials
Aerothermochemical coupling in boundary layers at high enthalpy
Multiscale methods for gas-surface interaction kinetics
impact: Improves predictive models for thermal protection systems
Informs material selection and design for extreme environments
Enables joint experiments and simulation campaigns with hypersonics groups
Hypersonic & Reentry Physics.imgtitle: Inflatable aerodynamic decelerators and a crew-module geometry built with PyAMorph

Hypersonic & Reentry Physics.title: Thermal Protection System Simulations
Hypersonic & Reentry Physics.subtitle: Microstructure-Resolved Response of Porous Heat-Shield Materials
Hypersonic & Reentry Physics.overview: Heat shields are porous, fibrous materials whose behaviour is set at the scale of individual fibres. We build fibre-felt microstructures, compute their effective thermal and transport properties, and simulate heat conduction, flow through the pores and material response directly on the resolved geometry.
currentProjects: Effective thermal properties of porous fibrous materials from meso-scale simulations
Synthetic and CT-derived fibre-felt microstructures
Coupled conduction and pore-scale flow in resolved microstructures
Material-response models for ablative heat shields
impact: Material properties computed from the microstructure rather than fitted
A link between micro-CT data and vehicle-scale heat-shield models
Support for reentry and hypersonic vehicle design
Hypersonic & Reentry Physics.imgtitle: Fibre-felt microstructures for thermal protection materials built with PyAMorph
